newsitem.title: USA: US Airways pilots file lawsuit vs company.
newsitem.headline: US Airways pilots file lawsuit vs company.

text.p: The pilots of US Airways Group Inc said Thursday they filed a lawsuit against the company, alleging that management's recent actions and statements "are intended to subvert and impair" contract negotiations.
US Airways, the nation's sixth largest airline, has been in labor talks with its pilots since their contract became amendable in April 1996.

The lawsuit, which was filed in federal district court in Pittsburgh, seeks injunctive relief against "further improper conduct," as well as damages under the Railway Labor Act, the federal statute that governs the airline industry's labor relations.

US Airways has laid off pilots and threatened additional layoffs, base closings, downsizing and cancellation of aircraft orders if the pilots do not comply with management's position for a new contract, the union said in its lawsuit.

US Airways also reiterated these comments in a series of letters and a videotape sent to pilots' homes, allegedly violating the federal law which requires management to deal with the pilots' union and not negotiate directly with or threaten the pilots, the union said.
US Airways' actions are intended "to unduly influence the outcome of negotiations," the union charged.
The union also cited US Airways' recent "road shows" with employees, in which the company outlined its competitive and financial challenges, as an indirect attempt to pressure contract talks.
US Airways told shareholders at its recent annual meeting that without a cost-cutting pact with the unionized employees, its growth remains hold.
US Airways, which has among the highest costs in the airline industry, faces growing competition from low-cost carriers.
Analysts estimate the airline needs up to $1.5 billion in wage, salary and productivity concessions to bring its costs in line with those of other carriers.
The union said that it will continue to seek "an amicable and reasonable solution to our bargaining differences, while pursuing our legal options."
US Airways said the union's lawsuit makes "unfounded" and "frivolous" allegations.
